title: Cancer-associated fibroblast-derived extracellular vesicles facilitate metastasis in hepatocellular carcinoma by delivering CTGF.
authors: Zheng, Mengli; Liu, Luyao; Cui, Haochen; Zhao, Yuchong; Chen, Wei; Bai, Shuya; Peng, Wang; Wang, Yun; Li, Yanling; Wang, Ronghua; Wang, Xiju; Cheng, Bin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CAF来源细胞外囊泡递送CTGF激活Notch1/Snail1通路促进肝癌转移，仅用分子对接辅助验证蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: PURPOSE: The tumor microenvironment (TME) plays a crucial role in cancer progression. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are key components of the TME and play critical roles in tumor development and metastasis. However, the mechanisms by which CAFs influence hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) metastasis are not fully understood. METHODS: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) from CAFs and normal fibroblasts (NFs) were characterized via western blotting, transmission electron microscopy, and nanoparticle tracking analysis. An iTRAQ-based proteomic sequencing analysis was conducted to quantify proteins in the EVs from these cells. Colony formation assays and Transwell assays were used to assess tumor cell proliferation and migration. Xenograft tumor models were established in nude mice to evaluate tumor progression in vivo. Coimmunoprecipitation and molecular docking were performed to explore the interactions between CTGF and Notch1. RESULTS: A high CAF abundance is associated with poor prognosis in HCC patients. EVs from CAFs significantly enhanced the proliferative and invasive abilities of HCC cells in vitro and in vivo. Connective tissue growth factor (CTGF) was found to be highly upregulated in CAF-derived EVs, and CTGF knockdown in CAF-derived EVs attenuated their tumor-promoting capacities. Mechanistically, CTGF derived from CAF-EVs activated the Notch1/Snail1 signaling pathway in recipient cells via interaction with the Notch1 receptor, enhancing HCC cell proliferation and invasion. Furthermore, high CTGF expression was significantly correlated with poor clinicopathological features in HCC patients. CONCLUSION: Our findings revealed that CTGF derived from CAF-EVs promoted the proliferation and invasion of HCC cells via activation of the Notch1/Snail1 pathway, highlighting CTGF derived from CAF-EVs as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in HCC.
abstract_zh: 目的：肿瘤微环境（TME）在癌症进展中发挥关键作用。癌症相关成纤维细胞（CAFs）是TME的重要组成部分，在肿瘤发展和转移中扮演关键角色。然而，CAFs影响肝细胞癌（HCC）转移的机制尚未完全阐明。方法：通过蛋白质印迹法、透射电子显微镜和纳米颗粒追踪分析对来自CAFs和正常成纤维细胞（NFs）的细胞外囊泡（EVs）进行表征。采用基于iTRAQ的蛋白质组学测序分析来定量这些细胞来源的EVs中的蛋白质。使用集落形成实验和Transwell实验评估肿瘤细胞增殖和迁移能力。在裸鼠中建立异种移植肿瘤模型以评估体内肿瘤进展。通过免疫共沉淀和分子对接探讨CTGF与Notch1之间的相互作用。结果：高CAF丰度与HCC患者的不良预后相关。来自CAFs的EVs在体外和体内显著增强了HCC细胞的增殖和侵袭能力。结缔组织生长因子（CTGF）在CAF来源的EVs中高度上调，且CAF来源的EVs中CTGF敲低减弱了其促肿瘤能力。机制上，CAF-EVs来源的CTGF通过与Notch1受体相互作用激活受体细胞中的Notch1/Snail1信号通路，从而增强HCC细胞的增殖和侵袭。此外，高CTGF表达与HCC患者的不良临床病理特征显著相关。结论：我们的研究结果表明，CAF-EVs来源的CTGF通过激活Notch1/Snail1通路促进HCC细胞的增殖和侵袭，强调CAF-EVs来源的CTGF可作为HCC的预后生物标志物和治疗靶点。
